newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk state shares rally on privatisation news.
newsitem.headline: Turk state shares rally on privatisation news.

text.p: Turkish stocks picked up in the afternoon session on Monday amid selective buying led by largely state owned shares due to remarks by Turkey's new privatisation chief, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 index jumped to 2,036 at 1222 GMT in mid-session, up 3.19 percent from Friday and compared to a 1.17 percent rise in the morning.
"Activity was confined to state shares, namely Eregli and did not spill over to other issues. Privatisation news positively affected the market," said Murat Turgut from Bab Securities.
The most heavily traded stocks in the second session were Eregli, up 2,000 lira at 27,500 and state-owned petroleum products marketer Petrol Ofisi, up 3,000 lira at 32,000.
The new acting chairman of Turkey's Privatisation Administration (OIB) said the sell-off programme would be revitalised after faltering during the change of government.
"There has been a delay of one month. We will continue our work at speed to make up for this delay," the OIB's Yalcin Atli told Reuters. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
